decisions.executionNote: Begin a gradual elbow-up approach to the red nut in the left workspace, lifting and pitching the left gripper while the right arm stays home.
Bring the left gripper vertically above the red nut, retaining the continuous elbow-up branch and clearance above the table.
Lower toward the red nut with a small camera-based centering correction; pause open at grasp height to verify alignment.
Center the red nut between the fingertips, close fully, and make a short lift to check retention visually.
The red nut stayed between the fingers during the lift. Raise it clear and carry it above the red bolt for wrist-view alignment.
Lower the retained red nut toward the matching upright bolt, with a small lateral centering correction; inspect engagement before turning.
Make a controlled clockwise tightening stroke on the red pair, maintaining a closed grasp and a slight downward thread-following motion.
Release the red nut on its bolt, reset wrist rotation without unscrewing it, and close again for another tightening stroke.
Continue clockwise tightening of the red nut, following the thread slightly downward, then release for wrist reset.
Reset the open left wrist for the next clockwise stroke, leaving the red nut on its bolt, then regrasp.
Apply a third clockwise stroke to advance the red nut down its matching bolt, then open the gripper while keeping the pair undisturbed.
Reset the open wrist without backing out the red nut, then regrasp for further tightening; the nut remains visibly aligned over its bolt.
Advance the red nut with a fourth clockwise stroke and release it for inspection, keeping the bolt axis and gripper position aligned.
Reset the open wrist for one more red tightening stroke, then regrasp the nut without translating the pair.
Apply a final controlled clockwise stroke to the red nut and open the gripper, leaving the pair on the table for visual inspection.
Withdraw open from the red pair, reset the wrist, and move above the gray nut on the left with table clearance.
Approach the gray nut from above using calibrated head-view centering; stop open just above grasp height to refine from the wrist image.
Refine gray-nut centering from the wrist image, descend to grasp height, close, and perform a short retention-check lift.
The gray nut remains between the fingers after lifting. Raise it above the other pieces and begin carrying it toward the center for a table-mediated handover.
Carry the retained gray nut to the middle without crossing arms, then lower toward a central placement for the right arm to retrieve.
Set the gray nut down in the middle, release it, and lift the left gripper clear before the right-arm pickup.
Move the left arm clear toward the purple nut while beginning the right arm's gradual elbow-up approach to the central gray nut; keep the workspaces separated.
Refine the left approach over the purple nut while bringing the right gripper upright and inward toward the gray pickup, maintaining arm separation.
Lower the left gripper around the purple nut with a wrist-image lateral correction, and bring the right gripper above the central gray nut for final visual alignment.
Finish the purple-nut grasp and make a small retention-check lift with the left arm. Lower the right gripper to the central gray nut, remaining open for alignment verification.
Lift the visibly retained purple nut clear on the left. Refine the right gray-nut grasp, close fully, and lift slightly to check retention before moving out of the center.
Carry the retained gray nut upward and out to its right-side bolt. Advance the purple nut toward the middle only as the right arm clears, with both grippers closed and ample separation.
Bring the purple nut to the central staging position while lowering the retained gray nut toward its bolt; pause near engagement to check the wrist-view alignment.
Lower the purple nut to the central staging surface. Seat the gray nut over its matching bolt and begin a clockwise tightening stroke with the right gripper closed.
Release the purple nut in the center and withdraw the left arm. The gray bolt appears laterally offset in the wrist view; make a small lifted recentering adjustment before further tightening.
Refine gray-nut centering toward the visible bolt tip and resume a short clockwise stroke. Move the open left arm safely back into its own workspace.
Leave the gray nut on its bolt while resetting the open right wrist for another clockwise stroke. Begin returning the empty left arm toward home along its continuous elbow-up path.
Apply another clockwise stroke to the now visually centered gray nut and release. Continue the empty left arm gently toward its home pose without changing elbow branch.
Settle the left arm at home. Reset the open right wrist without reversing the gray nut, then regrasp for another clockwise tightening stroke.
Continue tightening the aligned gray nut clockwise with slight downward thread following, then open the right gripper. Keep the left arm at home.
Reset the open right wrist while leaving the gray pair undisturbed, then regrasp for the next clockwise tightening stroke.
Apply a fourth clockwise tightening stroke to the gray nut, following the thread gently downward, and release while preserving alignment.
The gray nut is visibly advanced over its bolt. Reset the open right wrist and regrasp for one final controlled tightening stroke.
Finish the gray pair with one more clockwise stroke, then release the nut. Keep the left arm at home and inspect before withdrawing.
Withdraw the open right gripper from the gray pair, reset its yaw, and move above the centrally staged purple nut with table clearance.
Lower the open right gripper over the centrally staged purple nut, using its head-view position and the previous central pickup as a starting alignment; inspect before closing.
Refine the purple-nut alignment from the wrist view, descend to grasp height, close fully, and make a short lift to verify retention.
The purple nut remains between the fingers after the lift. Carry it upward and rightward, clearing the gray pair en route to its matching purple bolt.
Bring the purple nut above its matching bolt and lower to a cautious pre-insertion height, keeping the grasp closed while checking axis alignment from the wrist view.
Make a small wrist-image centering correction and lower the purple nut to the bolt entrance; pause closed to inspect engagement before turning.
The purple bolt tip is now centered within the nut. Apply the first clockwise tightening stroke with gentle downward thread following, then release for wrist reset.
The purple nut tipped rather than staying threaded. Withdraw open and reset the wrist, allowing it to settle so its pose can be assessed for recovery.
The purple nut has settled upright beside the bolt. Approach its new position open for a fresh, centered pickup rather than continuing the failed insertion.
Center the recovered purple nut between the right fingertips, lower to the established pickup height, close fully, and make a small lift to check the new grasp.
The recovered nut is still slightly high in the wrist view. Recenter the open fingertips, reclose at pickup height with more settling time, and lift to verify retention.
Retention of the recovered purple nut is uncertain. Reopen and change the right wrist yaw for more clearance from the gray pair, then approach again open for precise centering.
With the jaws now clear of the gray pair, correct the purple nut's lateral offset, close at pickup height, and lift vertically to verify the recovered grasp.
The purple nut now moves with the gripper. Lift it clear, make a small upright-axis correction, and position it above the purple bolt for a slower second insertion attempt.
Lower the retained purple nut slowly while correcting the bolt's lateral offset in the wrist image. Stop before rotation to verify the second insertion is truly centered.
The purple bolt is laterally centered but still appears ahead of the nut opening. Shift the retained nut toward it along the other horizontal axis and lower slightly, without turning yet.
The purple bolt tip is now inside the nut opening. Make a tiny lateral correction and a slow, short clockwise pilot stroke to test thread engagement without forcing it.
The pilot stroke reveals a small lateral offset of the purple bolt within the opening. Correct it by a few millimeters and continue only a short, slow turn to avoid tipping the nut again.
Pause rotation and make a small isolated lateral alignment correction to the purple nut, using the offset between the visible bolt and nut axes to check the direction before continuing.
The isolated correction improved lateral centering. Lower the purple nut a few millimeters without turning to establish deeper engagement, then inspect for any tilt or obstruction.
The purple nut still shows an offset rather than clean engagement. Back off vertically, then test a small correction along the remaining horizontal axis without further rotation.
Lift straight up with the right gripper closed to verify whether the purple nut is actually retained and clear the bolt before further alignment attempts.

The straight lift confirms that the purple nut is retained but sits unusually low in the grasp. With clearance above the bolt, isolate a horizontal-axis adjustment to bring the bolt beneath the actual nut opening rather than the nominal gripper center.
The isolated adjustment brought the purple bolt toward the held nut's axis. Lower slowly without rotation to inspect whether this corrected alignment permits clean entry.

The purple nut appears aligned but is held off-center, which would make rotation sweep it sideways. Seat and release it, then lift and reposition the open gripper over the nut's actual axis for a centered regrasp.
The purple nut did not stay on the bolt. Reapproach its newly visible tabletop position with a clearer jaw orientation and a centered grasp-height target; keep the other completed pairs undisturbed.
Use the open-wrist image to center the purple nut between the jaws, close with settling time, and make a short vertical lift to verify a centered grasp.
The purple nut is retained with a more centered grasp. Lift it clear and carry it above the matching bolt while preserving the wrist orientation for precise two-axis alignment.
Correct the purple bolt's lateral offset in the wrist image and lower the retained nut slowly to the entrance, keeping yaw fixed to distinguish alignment from grasp eccentricity.
The bolt is laterally centered but still offset along the other horizontal axis. Make a small isolated correction with the nut held and no rotation to bring the bolt cap under the opening.

The purple bolt now fills the opening without a visible table gap. Seat slightly deeper and make a slow clockwise stroke, compensating the small grasp offset with an arc so the nut stays over the bolt.
Continue the slow clockwise stroke around the estimated purple-nut axis, maintaining the grasp-offset compensation and following the thread downward before inspecting again.

The purple opening is still not convincingly concentric after the turn. Release and withdraw straight up to inspect whether the nut stayed on the bolt, rather than continuing to rotate against the offset.

The purple nut is again separate on the table. Re-estimate its center from the clear head view and approach with an upright wrist and open jaws, correcting accumulated orientation error before another centered pickup.
Use the wrist view rather than an assumed object height: correct the purple nut's clear lateral offset and descend open, then inspect the remaining centering error before closing.

The lateral correction is now centered. Correct the remaining fore-aft offset while reaching pickup height, close with settling time, and lift vertically to verify a genuinely centered purple-nut grasp.
The purple nut is now retained close to the gripper center. Lift above the bolt, carry it over the matching axis, and approach with fixed yaw so the next alignment can be assessed cleanly.
